slides.0.title: Oak Ageing and Age Statements
slides.0.subtitle: Oak casks, maturation aromas, and age statements such as VS, VSOP and XO
slides.1.title: Oak casks and maturation
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Cognac's oak
slides.1.highlights.0.content: At least two years in French oak, mainly Limousin and Tronçais (Wikipedia also lists Allier and Nevers); Limousin extracts tannin faster and more coarsely, Tronçais more slowly and subtly (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: New casks to old
slides.1.highlights.1.content: The usual practice is new casks first, then older ones to temper the oak; Difford's Guide says the spirit moves after about 18 months, and cask sizes differ by source so they are not tested
slides.1.highlights.2.title: The angels' share
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Spirit keeps evaporating during ageing: about 2% a year according to Wine With Seth and Difford's Guide, about 3% according to Wikipedia; very old Cognac can fall to about 40% abv
slides.1.content: Time and oak are the main sources of a brandy's colour, aroma and price.
slides.2.title: Cognac age grades
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The compte system
slides.2.highlights.0.content: The BNIC counts age from 1 April: freshly distilled spirit is Compte 00, becoming Compte 0 on 31 March and then gaining one each 1 April up to Compte 10 (Difford's Guide)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Minimum ages
slides.2.highlights.1.content: VS at least 2 years, VSOP at least 4, Napoléon at least 6, XO at least 10 (since April 2018) and XXO at least 14, judged by the youngest spirit in the blend (Wine With Seth, Wikipedia)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: The XO change
slides.2.highlights.2.content: The XO minimum rose from 6 to 10 years, first scheduled for 2016 but postponed for lack of stocks, and took effect in April 2018; the BNIC treats Hors d'âge as equal to XO (Wikipedia)
slides.2.content: Older sources often say XO is 6 years; use the post-2018 rule.
slides.3.title: Armagnac and adjustments
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Armagnac age statements
slides.3.highlights.0.content: VS 1 year, VSOP 4, Napoléon 6; a Millésimé must come 100% from the stated harvest and spend at least 10 years in oak (alcademics, WSET Level 2 guide). XO is given as 6 or 10 years by the two sources, so it is not tested
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Blanche d'Armagnac
slides.3.highlights.1.content: An unaged white spirit recognised by the AOC since 2005, rested at least three months in inert containers such as stainless steel
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Reduction and additives
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Cognac is reduced to about 65% before casking, with distilled water or petites eaux added in stages; caramel for colour, a little sugar and boisé (oak extract) are allowed (Difford's Guide)
slides.3.content: Adjustments are fine-tuning, not a change in the nature of the spirit.
What is the minimum age of a Cognac VSOP?
Compte 4, i.e. 4 years (Wine With Seth, Wikipedia).
Since when has the Cognac XO minimum been 10 years?
April 2018 (first scheduled for 2016, postponed for stocks).
How does the BNIC treat Hors d'âge?
C. It must be over 50 years
Wikipedia: in practice producers often use it for products above the official scale.
On which date does the compte age turn over?
It increases by one each 1 April (Difford's Guide).
How long must a Millésimé Armagnac spend in oak at minimum?
At least 10 years and 100% from that harvest.
